title: I Enforced the Food-Delivery Photo Rule After They Left It at 4B

parts.text: I watched the app camera ping at 7:19 p.m. with a photo of someone else's wreath. I live in 4A. The bag was at 4B. I was twenty-five, hungry after a late shift, holding a phone and a building fob. 4B is a man who works nights and does not answer. The app said delivered. The photo rule, which the company brags about, is supposed to match the pin. I uploaded the wreath mismatch and the 4A number plate I stuck beside my door last month for this exact genre of evening. At 7:24 the driver messaged I can see you in the hall, just take it, while still sitting in the lot.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He wants me to take 4B's wreath photo as delivered while he sits in the lot.

social.video_title: The delivery photo was a wreath I do not own — Part 1/2
social.description: 4A versus 4B, a bragged-about camera. He watched from the lot. Would you have grabbed the bag anyway?

parts.text: I did not enter 4B. Support reassigned a redelivery and dinged the photo fail. The second driver read the number plate. I ate noodles that were only somewhat late. 4B's wreath remained festive and unfed. The app still brags. I still have a plate. Pins are not vibes. Hallways are not a pickup window. I tipped the second driver because literacy is rare and hot.
